intended_object: Given a precoverage K on a category C, the associated family of conditions on pre-0-hypercovers (indexed covering families {Eᵢ → X}): a family E is admissible exactly when the presieve it generates belongs to K(X). This comes from the docstring and from its use as the forward map of `Precoverage.equivPreZeroHypercoverFamily`.
explanation:
The body sets `property X E := E.presieve₀ ∈ K X`. So a pre-0-hypercover of X counts as admissible exactly when its underlying presieve (the set of arrows `E.f i`) is a K-covering presieve. This is the obvious and correct translation.

The required field `iff_shrink` (the condition does not change under deduplication) holds automatically. Deduplicating a family does not change the presieve it generates, and `simp` proves it from that fact.

The construction works for an arbitrary category C with no extra hypotheses, so it is not too narrow. It is the forward direction of the equivalence `Precoverage.equivPreZeroHypercoverFamily`, and the inverse there is `PreZeroHypercoverFamily.precoverage`. Mathlib has no other declaration for the same construction.
